# Workshop programme {.unnumbered}

This book is a comprehensive, self-paced course consisting of 24 teaching units. A selection of 10 units is covered during a 3-day workshop. This page outlines the programme, detailing which units are taught in person and the order in which they are presented.

Each unit in the book, whether taught in the workshop or not, includes a complete chapter, a slide deck, an interactive Pluto notebook, and exercises with solutions. Attending the workshop offers in-person instruction, discussion, and debugging assistance for the 10 units. The remaining 14 units are fully developed and available for self-study, allowing you to work through them at your own pace, whether before, during, or after the workshop.

Each taught session also has a worksheet: a short set of exercises that build on what the session showed, with hints and answer checks. Worksheets live in the `worksheets/` folder of the repository, and worked solutions are added there at the end of each day.

## What the workshop covers

The ten sessions move in the following order: deterministic foundations and a first stochastic model; then stochastic dynamics in continuous time, the data a model produces, and what those data can identify; then decisions and individual-based models.

- **Day 1: foundations and discrete time.** A Julia primer, the SIR model derived from first principles, the `OrdinaryDiffEq` workflow, and discrete-time models, deterministic and stochastic.
- **Day 2: stochasticity, observation, and sensitivity.** Continuous-time jump processes, stochastic differential equations, observation models with simulated data, and sensitivity and identifiability.
- **Day 3: decisions and individual-based models.** Interventions and optimisation, then agent-based models.

The workshop deliberately stops before parameter estimation and Bayesian inference ([ch08](chapters/08-parameter-estimation.html), [ch09](chapters/09-bayesian-inference.html)). For those interested in fitting models to data and inference, we recommend having a look at the modelling course ["Model Fitting and Inference for Infectious Disease Dynamics"](https://www.lshtm.ac.uk/study/courses/short-courses/infectious-diseases-dynamics).

## Before the workshop

Please arrive with Julia, VS Code, and Quarto already installed and the course
packages downloaded. Installing takes far longer than the fifteen-minute
environment check on the first morning.

[**Setting up**](setup.qmd) walks through it step by step, including what to do
when something does not work. Allow about half an hour, most of it waiting for
downloads, and do it on a good connection rather than on workshop wifi.

No prior Julia experience is assumed: Day 1 starts at the REPL. If you would
like to read ahead, [Probability and stochastic
processes](prerequisites/02-probability-and-stochastic-processes.html) and
[Calculus and numerical
methods](prerequisites/03-calculus-and-numerical-methods.html) are useful
background, but they are optional: everything the sessions depend on is
recapped in the session that uses it.

## Schedule

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Days 1 and 2 run 09:30–17:30; Day 3 runs 09:30–16:00. Each day has a mid-morning or mid-afternoon break and lunch. Day 3 has a longer lunch and a closing block. Ten 90-minute sessions total 15 hours of teaching within 22.5 hours of contact time; the remaining time covers welcome and wrap-up, breaks, and lunch.
:::

## Self-study

The chapters and appendices listed below are not part of the workshop, but they can be organised as follows:

**Background** : Optional further material behind the workshop sessions. Neither is a prerequisite.

- [Probability and stochastic processes](prerequisites/02-probability-and-stochastic-processes.html) : Waiting times, memorylessness, and the binomial chain used in the stochastic sessions.
- [Calculus and numerical methods](prerequisites/03-calculus-and-numerical-methods.html) : The Euler method and order of convergence behind the ODE session.

**Connecting models to data, in depth** : Although we suggest that people interested in parameter estimation and Bayesian inference should look at the "Model Fitting and Inference for Infectious Disease Dynamics" course, the following three chapters provide a more detailed look at the topic.

- [Frequentist parameter estimation](chapters/08-parameter-estimation.html)
- [Bayesian inference](chapters/09-bayesian-inference.html)
- [Data-to-decision capstone](chapters/12-data-to-decision-capstone.html)

**Advanced extensions** : Each chapter builds on a taught session.

- [Delay differential equations](appendices/01-delay-differential-equations.html) : Generalises the memoryless recovery assumption used in the ODE, jump-process, and SDE sessions.
- [Stochastic delay differential equations](appendices/02-stochastic-delay-differential-equations.html) : Recombines that fixed delay with the stochastic differential equations session.
- [Discrete-event simulation](appendices/03-discrete-event-simulation.html) : Combines the jump-process and agent-based sessions into one individual-level, continuously-timed simulation.
- [Universal differential equations](appendices/04-universal-differential-equations.html) and [Surrogate and emulator models](appendices/07-surrogate-models.html) : Scientific machine learning.
- [Finite-state projection](appendices/05-finite-state-projection.html) : Extends the jump-process session by solving directly for the probability distribution instead of simulating trajectories.
- [Probabilistic numerical integration](appendices/06-probabilistic-numerical-integration.html) : Extends the ODE session by quantifying the solver's own numerical uncertainty.
- [Advanced optimal control](appendices/08-advanced-optimal-control.html) : Extends the interventions session.
- [Model composition and structured populations](appendices/09-model-composition.html) : Extends the stochastic differential equations session, composing structured, multi-group populations.

See the [course resources page](resources.qmd) for book, slide, and notebook links grouped by track.
